title: Self-check workbook: core/extended split, optional extended, human-readable variable dictionary
goal: Move every non-yellow-marked key of the self-check workbook 'result' sheet to a new optional 'extended' sheet; keep the check runnable in a simplified mode without that sheet; make the color marking (core set) explicit in code; give every key a human-readable description in Excel and in the GUI.

changes.summary: Core/extended split of the self-check workbook. CORE_RESULT_KEYS = the 10 yellow-marked cells of the reference workbook (f_value, coefficients.b0..b2, coefficients_v.b0..b2, t_tests.t0..t2). Writer emits 'result' (core, yellow fill) + 'extended' (rest); reader merges 'extended' when present and resolves the mode from the file; verify() gained mode=MODE_SIMPLIFIED (core fields only) vs MODE_FULL (every known field required); the reverse GUI verifies in the simplified mode by default, switches to extended automatically when the file carries an 'extended' sheet, and offers a Mode selector (Auto / Simplified / Extended); nts/dictionary.py adds the human description of every variable (RU + EN), written to a new 'description' column of the result/extended sheets, to a 'dictionary' sheet with the full glossary, and shown in a Description column of the reverse checklist; GUI exporter delegates to nts.checker.write_self_check_xlsx (removed ~70 duplicated lines); CLI forces UTF-8 stdout/stderr (the CLI used to die with UnicodeEncodeError on a cp1252 console).

verification.tests_passed: 79 passed (python -m pytest -q); new: 15 tests for the core/extended split, the optional 'extended' sheet, the simplified/full modes, the description column, the dictionary sheet and the reverse-GUI mode resolution
manual_checks: CLI: examples/default_result.xlsx -> 54 passed / exit 0; examples/default_result_core.xlsx -> 10 passed / exit 0; examples/default_with_expected.json -> 54 passed / exit 0
reverse GUI smoke: core-only workbook -> 10 rows (simplified), workbook with 'extended' -> 54 rows (auto-extended), forced simplified -> 10 rows, description column localized (RU/EN)
main GUI smoke: output panel renders the description under every value, in the current language
GUI export end-to-end: the button writes a 7-sheet workbook with the description column and the dictionary sheet; the exported file passes the self-check (54/54)

fulfills_ac: result sheet contains only the yellow-marked (core) keys; the rest move to the 'extended' sheet
core value cells keep the yellow fill; extended cells stay unstyled
a workbook without an 'extended' sheet passes the self-check in the simplified mode (10 core checks, exit 0)
a workbook with an 'extended' sheet is checked in the extended mode (54 checks, exit 0)
the simplified mode reports the main fields only — the optional G-test / output-row fields are not checked
the reverse GUI defaults to the simplified mode and switches to extended automatically when an 'extended' sheet is present
every key keeps its name and gains a human description: a 'description' column in Excel and a Description column in the GUI checklist
the GUI 'Export to Excel' produces the same layout as nts.checker.write_self_check_xlsx

notes.dependency_audit: Dependency graph taken from .temp/расчет.xlsx (Лист2 formulas). The core values are NOT self-contained as data: f_value needs f_avg (extended), coefficients_v.* need z_averages.*/pz.* (extended), t_tests.* additionally need S_в (N14), which is not exported at all. Making 'extended' optional is still safe because compute() rebuilds the whole model from the 'input' sheet and verify() compares field-by-field — the dependency chain lives on the computation side, not on the verification side.
notes.mode_resolution: Workbook: 'extended' sheet present -> extended mode, otherwise simplified. JSON payload: the 'expected' block is a complete ComputeResult -> extended mode. The reverse GUI's Mode selector overrides the automatic choice.
notes.reference_file: examples/default_result.xlsx is data-identical to the hand-made reference workbook (all 26 result keys, input, criteria, grubbs, output_rows match) — only the sheet split and the descriptions differ. The original file itself was left untouched.
